response.markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a small diagnostic that compares earlier-order and endpoint-randomizing interventions without changing the trained GRU4Rec.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Earlier deletion probes reported substantial padded-versus-unpadded score differences. Fixed-length shuffles preserve padding placement but still require execution checks. (2) Anonymous loader rows cannot support user-cluster uncertainty. Explicit user-indexed prefixes enable equal-user summaries; deterministic selection does not justify population coverage. (3) Strong training-pair margins do not establish held-out ranking quality. The failed trial’s subprocess traceback does not identify its underlying error.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Saturated GRU gates can preserve state [1]; gate statistics alone cannot establish lost temporal credit. (2) Perturbation rankings vary with intervention and region size [2]. Its time-series classification findings motivate controls but do not validate recommendation shuffles. (3) Sampled metrics can disagree with catalog rankings [3]. Diagnostic ranks remain separate from official validation. (4) Dependency-breaking permutations can create unrealistic inputs [4]. Sensitivity measures a specified intervention distribution, not causal intent.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Observable evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Execution integrity | Repeatability, padding placement, scorer parity | Correct execution does not prove usefulness |
| Temporal sensitivity | Fixed-length paired interventions | Different shuffle distributions do not isolate endpoint importance |
| Retrieval fidelity | Frozen-candidate and catalog ranks | Training-prefix ranks do not establish generalization |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Fixed-final paired shuffle panel: 4/7/4.** Originality: + integrates execution and uncertainty controls; − established methods. Potential: + inexpensive temporal evidence; − conditional, shifted inputs. Difficulty: + existing hooks; − tie parity, sampling and uncertainty require care [2,4–6].
2. **Chunked catalog competition audit: 3/7/4.** Originality: + connects sampled and catalog failures; − standard audit. Potential: + reveals candidate sensitivity; − cannot replace the benchmark. Difficulty: + no retraining; − catalog scoring costs time [3].
3. **Lag-gradient/intervention agreement: 5/6/6.** Originality: + triangulates recurrent credit; − familiar attribution. Potential: + guides recurrent changes; − gradients need not predict finite interventions. Difficulty: + one checkpoint; − faithful instrumentation requires care [1,2].
4. **Matched endpoint/prefix transpositions: 4/7/5.** Originality: + tighter perturbation matching; − standard swaps. Potential: + controls changed-position count; − transitions still differ. Difficulty: + same scorer; − eligible matching can be sparse [4].

**Selected idea: fixed-final paired shuffle panel.** Freeze one training-prefix target and 99 unique negatives per eligible user. Compare intact histories, uniform full shuffles and uniform final-fixed prefix shuffles. Preserve multiplicities, length and padding; record changed positions, endpoint changes and unchanged inputs. With n items and m endpoint-item occurrences, full shuffling preserves endpoint identity with probability m/n. The contrast compares intervention distributions, not isolated last-item importance; weak prefix effects do not exclude unordered history use.

Average five independent draws within users. Report rank damage, score margins and ties; withhold ranks without the pinned tie rule. Separate finite-permutation MCSE from paired user-bootstrap reweighting intervals [5,6]. Preserve interfaces, RNG states and one checkpoint/category. Diagnose in-sample sensitivity only; select training changes solely through unchanged macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Implement a reproducible fixed-length temporal-sensitivity panel for the supplied GRU4Rec, comparing intact histories with uniform full-history shuffles and uniform final-item-fixed prefix shuffles using the same trained model, target and candidate set. Interpret their contrast as a difference between intervention distributions rather than isolated final-item importance.
idea.motivation: Prior deletion diagnostics reported padding-dependent score changes, while sampled training margins supplied no held-out improvement evidence. Fixed-length shuffling preserves padding placement and item multiplicities, narrowing execution-related ambiguity without eliminating perturbation distribution shift. At early research progress, this is more feasible than recurrent instrumentation. It makes no unsupported claims about compatibility, mood, causal intent, harmful shortcuts or higher-order sequence understanding. Matched endpoint/prefix transpositions remain a useful subsequent control if the initial panel warrants further investigation.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Use the actual view.model and existing item_emb, log2feats and predict_score interfaces, including learned score biases. Preserve existing diagnostics and the five-per-category full-catalog unseen-item recommendation workflow for twenty real training users. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable categories, reviews, ratings, prices, stores and simulator traits must not be inferred.

Construct explicitly user-indexed diagnostic cases from user_train rather than attempting to recover user IDs from anonymous loader rows. Define a reproducible protocol: sort users by their serialized identifier, select the first at most 200 eligible users, use each user's final training interaction as the diagnostic target and all preceding training interactions as its prefix, then retain the latest interactions fitting the baseline external sequence width. Require at least five retained interactions. Targets remain training observations potentially seen during fitting, not new held-out examples. Save user ordering, raw and retained history lengths, truncation settings, target IDs, candidate IDs, category, selection rules and exclusion counts. Do not read host validation or hidden test files to construct cases.

Freeze each target plus 99 unique real-item negatives excluding the user's complete training history and target. Sample uniformly without replacement from the eligible real-item pool using a separate local seed-42 stream; report insufficient pools rather than relaxing uniqueness. Store the target first, preserve candidate order thereafter, and save exact candidate identities. These are diagnostic candidates, not host validation candidates. Persist artifacts beneath the trial directory.

Preserve external sequence width, nonpadding positions, padding placement and duplicate multiplicities. Gather the maximum nonzero position, never count minus one; skip empty histories. Use the documented ModelView NumPy adapter where required and convert outputs explicitly without changing scorer semantics. Verify finite outputs, shapes, repeated-call consistency, batch-order independence and batched-versus-single scoring. Verify the documented reset-state behavior; eval() alone does not reset carried recurrent state. Report padding invariance and empty-history behavior against the actual architecture contract rather than silently changing recurrence. Measure training/exported-predictor parity only if the exported callable is available; otherwise report unavailable. Disable temporal interpretation if required execution checks fail. No backbone implementation is supplied here, so previous padding findings must not be presumed to describe the current checkpoint.

For each user, draw five independent uniform position permutations for each intervention using separate local generators initialized by SeedSequence([42, stable_user_index, intervention_id]); use distinct namespace IDs for candidate sampling, interventions and bootstrap. Full shuffling permutes all nonpadding positions; fixed-final shuffling permutes all but the final nonpadding position. Always assign from an unchanged copy of the original sequence. Include identity and duplicate-induced unchanged draws in primary estimates; never redraw until changed. Record permutations, actual changed-position counts and fractions, endpoint-identity changes, unchanged-input rates, users with any changed draw, history length and endpoint-item multiplicity. Full shuffling preserves the original endpoint identity with probability m/n when it occurs m times among n retained items. Report observed endpoint-preservation rates alongside this expectation. Changed-draw conditional summaries remain separately labeled and can change the weighting and target estimand.

Use the pinned evaluator's exact ranking and tie convention when available; otherwise return rank and HR fields null with a reason while retaining score diagnostics. Record exact target-score ties, ties spanning the tenth-place boundary, positive-minus-negative score margins, target-versus-highest-negative margin and candidate-score changes. Tolerance-based near-ties are supplementary and never alter ranks. Define rank damage as perturbed rank minus original rank and hit damage as original HR@10 minus perturbed HR@10, so positive values consistently denote damage. Neither diagnostic HR@10 nor its intervention delta is official validation HR@10.

Define the estimand as the equally weighted selected-user mean expected damage under each specified random intervention distribution, conditional on the fitted checkpoint, retained histories and frozen candidates. Average five draws within each user, then average users equally. Calculate full-minus-fixed-final contrasts within users. Because the two intervention streams are independent, estimate each user's contrast Monte Carlo variance as s_full,u^2/5 + s_fixed,u^2/5; user pairing does not pair independent permutation draws. For U equally weighted users, intervention MCSE is sqrt(sum_u s_u^2/(5*U^2)); contrast MCSE is sqrt(sum_u (s_full,u^2+s_fixed,u^2)/(5*U^2)). For general weights w_u use sqrt(sum_u w_u^2*s_u^2/5). Five draws give noisy variance estimates: report the count, seeds and estimated MCSE without precise tail-coverage claims. A future valid shared-randomness coupling would instead require variance of draw-wise differences to retain covariance.

Bootstrap complete user records with all draws and conditions retained, using 2,000 seed-42 replicates and identical resampled user indices across conditions. Require at least 30 complete users for intervals; otherwise return null with a reason. Do not bootstrap permutations again within users. Label percentile intervals as empirical selected-user reweighting intervals conditional on realized draws, checkpoints and candidates. Deterministic selection provides no probability-sampling basis for population coverage, unseen-user generalization or causal inference. Report Monte Carlo error separately; do not add bootstrap and Monte Carlo uncertainties as though they were independent variance components. Provide descriptive history-length and repeat-target slices with denominators and small-slice warnings.

A category-local probe returns macro fields null. Aggregate only when all four category outputs are available, using equal category weights and independent within-category user resampling. For independent category streams, macro MCSE is sqrt(sum_c MCSE_c^2)/4. Save category summaries and per-user records for this external aggregation. Uncertainty excludes retraining, training-seed variation and candidate resampling; candidates are fixed by design.

Use torch.inference_mode(), preserve every module's training flag and Python, NumPy, Torch and CUDA RNG states, and restore them in finally. No architecture or predictor change is proposed: each category retains exactly one independently trained GRU4Rec checkpoint, without independent scorers, fusion or averaging. Preserve all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution and trial-local artifacts. If later architecture changes are authorized, update training, ModelView, checkpoint configuration and the embedded predictor writer together and retrain consistently. Log diagnostic runtime and all adaptive search exposure within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Prespecify this panel rather than adjusting users, candidates or interventions to obtain favorable results. Select subsequent training changes only with the unchanged host macro validation HR@10. No execution success or recommendation improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved_state = capture_all_module_training_flags_and_all_rng_states()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                existing = run_existing_family_specific_diagnostics(train_loader)
                checks = audit_documented_execution_contract(self.view)
                if not checks.required_checks_pass:
                    return merge_with_unavailable_temporal_metrics(existing, checks)

                # Explicit protocol: sorted user IDs, final training target,
                # preceding prefix truncated to baseline width, >=5 real items.
                cases = build_user_indexed_training_cases(
                    self.view.user_train, max_users=200,
                    target_rule='final_training_interaction',
                    order_rule='lexicographic_serialized_user_id',
                    minimum_retained_history=5,
                    width=baseline_external_width,
                    unique_negatives=99, seed=42,
                    exclude_complete_training_history=True)
                records = []
                for stable_index, case in enumerate(cases):
                    original_sequence = case.sequence.clone()
                    positions = nonzero_positions(original_sequence)
                    candidates = case.frozen_candidates

                    def score(sequence):
                        # Respect the existing NumPy/Tensor ModelView adapter.
                        states = compatible_log2feats(self.view, sequence)
                        last = maximum_nonzero_position_per_row(sequence)
                        features = gather_positional_features(states, last)
                        return self.view.predict_score(features, candidates)

                    original_scores = score(original_sequence)
                    record = initialize_user_record(case, original_scores)
                    for intervention_id, mode in enumerate(['full', 'fixed_final']):
                        rng = local_seed_sequence_rng(
                            42, stable_index, intervention_namespace + intervention_id)
                        movable = positions if mode == 'full' else positions[:-1]
                        for draw in range(5):
                            permutation = rng.permutation(len(movable))
                            altered = original_sequence.clone()
                            altered[movable] = original_sequence[movable[permutation]]
                            perturbed_scores = score(altered)
                            record.append(paired_diagnostics(
                                original_scores, perturbed_scores, candidates,
                                tie_rule=exact_host_tie_rule_or_none,
                                rank_damage='perturbed_rank-original_rank',
                                hit_damage='original_hit-perturbed_hit',
                                changed_positions=count_changed_positions(
                                    original_sequence, altered),
                                endpoint_changed=endpoint_identity_changed(
                                    original_sequence, altered),
                                unchanged=tensor_equal(original_sequence, altered),
                                permutation=permutation))
                    record.endpoint_preservation_expectation = (
                        count_endpoint_item_occurrences(original_sequence)
                        / len(positions))
                    records.append(record)

                save_trial_local_cases_candidates_configuration_and_draws(records)
                user_means = average_all_draws_within_user(records)
                summary = equal_user_means_and_within_user_contrasts(user_means)
                # Independent intervention streams: sum their MC variances.
                summary['mcse'] = independent_stream_mcse(records, draws=5)
                summary['reweighting_intervals'] = paired_user_bootstrap(
                    records, replicates=2000, seed=42, minimum_users=30,
                    preserve_all_draws=True, resample_draws=False)
                summary['changed_draw_conditional'] = separately_labeled_summary(records)
                summary['slices'] = descriptive_length_and_repeat_target_slices(records)
                summary['macro'] = None
                return merge_metrics_and_explicit_definitions(existing, checks, summary)
        finally:
            restore_all_module_training_flags_and_all_rng_states(saved_state)

# External aggregation requires exactly the four category outputs.
# Average categories equally; bootstrap users independently within categories.
# With independent streams: macro_mcse = sqrt(sum(category_mcse**2)) / 4.

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return interpretation_prompt_with_measured_metrics_and_definitions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        limits=['conditional fitted-model training-prefix sensitivity',
                'full-minus-fixed-final compares intervention distributions',
                'weak shuffle effects do not exclude unordered history use',
                'perturbation distribution shift',
                'selected-user reweighting intervals lack population coverage justification',
                'finite-permutation MCSE is reported separately',
                'fixed checkpoint and candidate conditioning',
                'no causal intent, harmful-shortcut or validation-improvement inference'])

originality.positive: Combines fixed-length final-item controls, execution checks, explicit intervention estimands and separated Monte Carlo and user-reweighting uncertainty in a focused GRU4Rec diagnostic.
originality.negative: Permutations, paired comparisons, variance propagation and user bootstrap methods are established; the contribution is an incremental integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides reproducible evidence for prioritizing later order-learning, endpoint-control or retrieval experiments while preserving the single-model constraint.
future_potential.negative: Artificial permutations of training prefixes cannot establish generalization or user intent, and further diagnostic refinement alone does not improve recommendation quality.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing feature and scoring interfaces without retraining, changing GRU internals or modifying the predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: The earlier score of 3 understated exact tie-rule parity, adapter compatibility, reproducible case construction, mode restoration, separate uncertainty calculations and cross-category aggregation.

related_work.title: [1] Improving the Gating Mechanism of Recurrent Neural Networks
contributions: Studies recurrent gating and motivates distinguishing state preservation from ease of learning.
Supports treating gate saturation as incomplete evidence about temporal credit.
limitations: Does not validate the supplied GRU4Rec checkpoint or establish recommendation improvements.
Gate observations omit the full recurrent derivative and target-ranking effects.

related_work.title: [2] Šimić, Veas and Sabol (2025): A comprehensive analysis of perturbation methods in explainable AI feature attribution validation for neural time series classifiers
contributions: Examines five datasets, five neural architectures, 12 attribution methods, 23 perturbation methods and two region sizes.
Shows that perturbation choice can change attribution rankings and that no method consistently dominates across settings.
Introduces the Consistency-Magnitude-Index and motivates comparing perturbation types, magnitudes and controls.
limitations: Studies neural time-series classification rather than categorical recommendation histories, ranking quality or HR@10.
Confidence collapse can reflect perturbation-induced distribution shift rather than feature importance.
Its findings motivate diagnostic controls but do not directly validate the proposed recommendation panel.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog evaluation and alter model comparisons.
Motivates separating fixed-candidate sensitivity diagnostics from catalog retrieval and official benchmark selection.
limitations: Does not determine this checkpoint's performance or replace the task's pinned selection metric.
A catalog audit on training prefixes remains conditional diagnostic evidence rather than held-out evaluation.

related_work.title: [4] Please Stop Permuting Features: An Explanation and Alternatives
contributions: Explains how permutation-based importance can break dependencies and create unrealistic inputs.
Motivates interpreting shuffle diagnostics relative to their specified intervention distributions.
limitations: General feature-permutation arguments do not establish the magnitude of distribution shift in this GRU4Rec task.
Preserving sequence length and item multiplicities does not preserve transition plausibility, temporal availability or endpoint context.

related_work.title: [5] Abadie et al.: Sampling-Based versus Design-Based Uncertainty in Regression Analysis
contributions: Distinguishes sources and interpretations of uncertainty under sampling and research design.
Motivates explicitly stating what selected-user resampling represents and what remains conditioned upon.
limitations: Does not directly derive confidence intervals for this sequential-recommendation diagnostic.
Bootstrapping deterministically selected users does not supply a probability-sampling justification for population coverage.

related_work.title: [6] Morris, White and Crowther (2019): Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
contributions: Emphasizes reproducible simulation design and reporting Monte Carlo uncertainty caused by finite repetitions.
Supports recording draw counts, seeds and Monte Carlo standard errors separately from other uncertainty summaries.
limitations: The diagnostic's MCSE formulas apply standard variance propagation rather than a recommendation-specific result from this paper.
Five repetitions yield noisy within-user variance estimates and do not support precise Monte Carlo tail-coverage claims.
